I once knew a guy who was compulsive liar and made up an entire imaginary friend. This wasn’t just a “Canadian girlfriend” situation, either, it was bizarrely elaborate, which made it easier to debunk. When we got suspicious about it, he claimed that they weren’t speaking to each other, and then he just never mentioned the imaginary friend again.The guy in question was in his 30’s, by the way.

(Edit: Thought I’d just post it.)

The liar’s name was Kevin. The imaginary friend’s name was Mike. Mike was the older brother of Kevin’s childhood BFF, David. David had died tragically several years ago, but Mike and Kevin still kept in touch.

Mike was a wealthy businessman who lived in a nearby city. He started working in the mailroom of a well-known company, but soon progressed through the ranks and was now one of the owners. He lived in a mansion. He owned a helicopter. He was so high-profile due to his job that he had body doubles that would show up to public functions in his place. He wrote a book under a pseudonym and gave Kevin a signed copy. He met his wife while walking through the park one day, in a situation that sounded like a plot out of a bad romantic comedy, and probably was.

This all sounds totally ridiculous (and it was), but nobody ever heard all of it at once. It was just little details, told to different people at different times, over the span of years. Kevin quite literally spent several years acting like this guy was totally real. He even pointed out the guy’s mansion one time. It was only after a few mutual friends and I were talking about it one afternoon that we decided to Google Mike’s full name and found nothing, except for a small-time motivational speaker on the other side of the country. Kevin wasn’t just embellishing a story, he had a whole imaginary friend.

I think somebody must have confronted Kevin about this because shortly after this revelation, Kevin claimed that he and Mike had some sort of fight, and weren’t speaking to each other. After that, Kevin never voluntarily brought him up again, like the whole thing never happened.

The icing on the cake is that years later, in a conversation about the Mike saga, two of my friends and I realized that we had all heard three entirely separate stories of how David died. One of them heard it was a tragic motorcycle accident. The other heard he was killed in a bar fight. I, the lucky person that I am, was told that David died of super-AIDS and his body was taken by the CDC. Yes, I’m serious.

Kevin was fucking weird.
